title: MM-MT101-GovernedSpawnToolSurface

scope.summary:
GOAL: Expose worker spawning to orchestrator-model sessions as ONE governed tool, `spawn_worker`, so a model can request a child worker session without gaining any new spawn authority. Today NO model-initiated spawn exists (verified: spawns come only from operator surfaces and the scheduler; CLI children have null stdin). This MT creates the first model-facing spawn surface and it MUST NOT create a second spawn path: the handler routes EXCLUSIVELY through SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session (src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/coordinator.rs, `pub async fn spawn_session`), which is the single sanctioned spawn path enforcing the concurrency semaphore cap, the monotonic lifetime spawn ceiling (HBR-SWARM-002 loop-cap semantics on `lifetime_spawns` / `budget.max_lifetime_spawns`), coordinator-minted checkout leases (ClaimLease / CheckoutLeaseRef), and CancellationToken teardown.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_tools/ (mod.rs + spawn_tool.rs + types.rs) registered from swarm_orchestration/mod.rs; a tool descriptor + JSON-schema for `spawn_worker`; a handler that (a) resolves the calling session's identity from the session tool channel (MT-007 session API seam), (b) evaluates the MT-106 model-to-model policy BEFORE any coordinator call, (c) builds a SpawnRequest with `parent_session_id` set to the calling session (field already exists in src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/ids.rs SpawnRequest), and (d) calls SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session. Plus unit/integration tests. No frontend changes.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Tool schema `spawn_worker` with input fields: `role_id` (string, must resolve against the MT-081/MT-086 role registry), `task_payload_ref` (string reference to a governed task payload — never inline free-text instructions; the payload body itself is fetched server-side and passes the MT-104 injection scan before delivery to the child), `lane_preference` (optional string, validated against ModelLaneStore lanes in src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs), `workspace_mode` (enum: `worktree` | `worktree_vm` | `none`), `budget` (object: max_child_tokens?, max_child_cost?, max_child_wall_secs? — all optional, all clamped to the MT-106 per-parent ceiling; a model can never raise its own ceiling).
2. Serve the tool on the session's tool channel as an MCP-server-style surface following the gate pattern of src/backend/handshake_core/src/mcp/gate.rs (GatedMcpClient / evaluate_kernel_tool_gate_decision / ConsentDecision): every call passes a deny-by-default gate decision before the handler body runs, and the decision (allow or deny, with reason) is recorded.
3. Parent identity is captured server-side from the authenticated session context — NEVER from tool arguments. A `parent_session_id` supplied inside tool arguments is rejected as a typed error (identity spoofing attempt, ledgered).
4. Policy check (MT-106) evaluated before spawn: parent role/session allowed to spawn requested role/lane, per-parent concurrent-children cap, per-parent budget ceiling, allowed workspace modes. No policy row => DENY (deny-by-default).
5. Typed rejections surfaced to the calling model as structured tool errors: `PolicyDenied` (MT-106 denial, with policy row id), `CapExceeded` (maps SwarmError::ConcurrencyCapReached / LifetimeSpawnCeilingReached / BudgetExhausted from src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/error.rs), `ConsentRequired` (cloud-lane spawn blocked pending operator consent per the model_runtime/cloud/consent_gate.rs consent surface). Rejections are terminal for the call — no silent retry loop inside the handler (HBR-SWARM-001 bounded-loop).
6. Every call — success AND rejection — writes a ledger row (process_ledger) attributing parent session, requested role, decision, and resulting child instance id when spawned, and stamps the existing FR-EVT-SWARM-SESSION-SPAWNED / FR-EVT-SWARM-SPAWN-REJECTED events (src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs SwarmFrEventId) with the parent attribution in the payload.

SECURITY FRAME (binding): model-initiated spawn is a privilege-escalation surface. This MT may not add any bypass of caps, ceilings, leases, consent gates, or breaker state; the coordinator's existing enforcement is the enforcement. Anthropic multi-agent research precedent: orchestrator-workers with structured spawn requests; Handshake adds the governed-tool + deny-by-default policy layer they describe as the safety gap.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read coordinator.rs spawn_session, ids.rs SpawnRequest, error.rs SwarmError, mcp/gate.rs gate evaluation, and the MT-007 session tool-channel seam.
2. Create model_tools/types.rs: SpawnWorkerInput, SpawnWorkerOutput { child_session_id, lane, workspace_mode, budget_granted }, ModelToolError { PolicyDenied, CapExceeded, ConsentRequired, InvalidInput, IdentitySpoofAttempt }.
3. Create model_tools/spawn_tool.rs: descriptor + JSON schema + handler as specced; handler takes &SwarmCoordinator and the MT-106 policy evaluator trait (define the trait here if MT-106 lands later; deny-by-default stub until a real evaluator is registered).
4. Wire the tool into the session tool channel registration (MT-007 seam) behind a config flag `model_to_model.spawn_tool_enabled` (default false = feature dark).
5. Ledger + FR event stamping with parent attribution.
6. Tests per expected_tests, including the no-second-spawn-path grep-level proof and deny-by-default proof.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs (payload attribution only; new event ids belong to MT-161)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (except named IPC/GUI surfaces for the GUI MT; this MT names none)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/coordinator.rs (read-only: the sanctioned spawn path must not be modified or forked by this MT)
acceptance_criteria: `spawn_worker` tool exists with the specced schema and is served on the session tool channel behind config flag model_to_model.spawn_tool_enabled (default false).
Handler calls SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session and NOTHING else creates sessions: no factory call, no process spawn, no duplicated cap/lease logic inside model_tools.
Parent identity comes only from authenticated session context; a parent_session_id inside tool arguments produces typed IdentitySpoofAttempt rejection plus a ledger row.
With no MT-106 policy row registered, every spawn_worker call is denied (deny-by-default) with PolicyDenied.
Coordinator rejections (concurrency cap, lifetime ceiling, budget) surface as typed CapExceeded tool errors — never as silent success, never retried in a loop inside the handler.
Cloud-lane spawns without operator consent surface ConsentRequired; consent gate is not bypassed.

Every call (allow and deny) produces a process_ledger row with parent attribution, and spawned children stamp FR-EVT-SWARM-SESSION-SPAWNED with parent_session_id in payload; rejections stamp FR-EVT-SWARM-SPAWN-REJECTED.
Budget in the request is clamped to the policy ceiling; a request above ceiling is granted at most the ceiling (recorded) or denied per policy config — it never passes through unclamped.
expected_tests: unit: spawn_worker schema validation rejects unknown fields, bad workspace_mode, inline parent_session_id
unit: deny-by-default with no policy evaluator registered
integration: policy-allowed spawn routes through spawn_session and returns child_session_id with ledger row + FR event
integration: coordinator cap exhaustion maps to CapExceeded typed error
integration: budget clamp to policy ceiling
negative: feature flag off => tool not listed on the channel
implementation_notes: Verified grounding: SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session at coordinator.rs (semaphore + cold_start_semaphore + lifetime_spawns AtomicU64 vs budget.max_lifetime_spawns + ClaimLease + CancellationToken); SpawnRequest already carries parent_session_id, role_id, owner_role, worktree_id, working_dir (ids.rs); SwarmError variants ConcurrencyCapReached / LifetimeSpawnCeilingReached / BudgetExhausted (error.rs); FR-EVT-SWARM-SESSION-SPAWNED and FR-EVT-SWARM-SPAWN-REJECTED exist in events.rs SwarmFrEventId.
The MT-106 policy evaluator is co-designed: define the evaluator trait in this MT (deny-by-default when unregistered); MT-106 supplies the real config-backed implementation.

task_payload_ref indirection is deliberate: free-text instruction bodies from a model never travel inline through the spawn surface; the referenced payload is injection-scanned (MT-104) before the child reads it.
Do not add new SwarmFrEventId variants here; new FR kinds are MT-161's seam. Reuse existing ids and enrich payloads only.
Cross-family seams (reference only, not authored here): MT-001 session model, MT-002 steer queue, MT-007 session API, MT-081/086 roles, MT-121 MT-signal contract.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend tool surface; operator visibility for the session tree ships in MT-107.

target_entries: Model-to-model orchestration: spawn_worker governed tool — what it is, deny-by-default policy, typed rejections, how the operator enables model_to_model.spawn_tool_enabled

risk_if_missed: No governed model-initiated spawn surface exists; either the capability is missing entirely (Anthropic-style orchestrator-workers impossible) or a later MT improvises an ungoverned spawn path bypassing caps/leases/consent — the exact privilege-escalation this WP exists to prevent.

risks: RISK-1: Second spawn path — the handler (or a test helper promoted to product code) creates sessions without SwarmCoordinator::spawn_session, silently bypassing semaphore cap, lifetime ceiling, leases, and breaker.
RISK-2: Identity spoofing — a model supplies parent_session_id / role_id attribution in tool arguments and the handler trusts it, corrupting lineage, policy evaluation, and ledger attribution.
RISK-3: Budget self-escalation — a parent passes a budget above its policy ceiling and the value flows unclamped into SpawnRequest, letting a model grant itself more than the operator allowed.
RISK-4: Prompt-injection via task payload — inline instruction text in the spawn call reaches the child unscanned, letting a compromised orchestrator inject instructions into workers.
RISK-5: Allow-by-default drift — a missing/unregistered policy evaluator silently allows spawns instead of denying them.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Executable proof target asserts model_tools/ contains a spawn_session call and NO factory/process-spawn symbols; coordinator.rs is a forbidden path for this MT.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Parent identity resolved exclusively from authenticated session context; argument-supplied identity is a typed, ledgered IdentitySpoofAttempt rejection with a dedicated test.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Budget clamp to policy ceiling with a test asserting the granted budget never exceeds the ceiling; granted value recorded in the ledger row.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): task_payload_ref indirection only — no inline instruction body accepted; payload passes MT-104 injection scan before child delivery (integration point named in tests).
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Deny-by-default when no evaluator is registered, proven by model_tools_spawn_denied_by_default test.
